proposal: The Mandate recommends that Congress eliminate disparate impact as a valid theory of discrimination under Title VII and other laws, that the President forbid OFCCP from using it, and that EEO-1 race and ethnicity data collection end (including by amending Title VII to bar it). It argues that such data and theories can push employers toward racial quotas.

status_summary: EO 14281 (2025-04-23) set a policy of eliminating disparate-impact liability to the extent possible and told agencies to deprioritize enforcing provisions that rely on it, including Title VII. Agencies have since acted administratively: EEOC reportedly closed disparate-impact-only charges by 2025-09-30, DOJ published a final rule on 2025-12-10 removing effects-based provisions from its Title VI regulations, DOJ issued a 2026-06-09 opinion questioning the constitutionality of disparate-impact liability under Title VII, and many other agencies removed disparate impact from their Title VI rules in 2026. EEOC proposed on 2026-07-23 to rescind the EEO-1 through EEO-6 reports (comments closed 2026-08-24); no final rule had been published through 2026-10-13. The statutory disparate-impact provision in Title VII is unchanged, and private plaintiffs and state agencies can still bring such claims.

timeline.event: President signs EO 14281, which states a policy of eliminating disparate-impact liability to the maximum extent possible, directs agencies to deprioritize enforcement of statutes and rules containing it (including Title VII), and directs the Attorney General to repeal or amend agencies' Title VI disparate-impact rules. It gives the Attorney General and EEOC Chair 45 days to review pending matters relying on the theory.

EEOC internal direction, reported by Bloomberg Law and summarized by a law firm on 2025-09-25, sets 2025-09-30 as the deadline to close almost all pending charges based only on disparate impact (charging parties receive right-to-sue notices). Charges that also allege disparate treatment stay open on that theory alone.

DOJ publishes a final rule (90 FR 57141), effective the same day and issued without prior notice and comment, removing the effects-based (disparate-impact) provisions from its Title VI regulations at 28 CFR 42.104 so they reach only intentional discrimination, citing Executive Order 14281.

DOJ issues a memorandum opinion (described by a law firm as from the Office of Legal Counsel) concluding that EEOC rules treating effects alone as discrimination, including the Uniform Guidelines on Employee Selection Procedures, are unconstitutional to that extent.

DOL publishes a final rule removing disparate-impact liability from its Title VI regulations; the Federal Register shows comparable final rules from other agencies between April and August 2026 (for example Commerce, Interior, Transportation, Agriculture, Education, HHS and others).
EEOC publishes a rule rescinding its 1979 Title VII affirmative action guidelines (a law-firm summary reports the Commission voted on 2026-06-30).

EEOC publishes a proposed rule to rescind the EEO-1 through EEO-6 reporting requirements and related recordkeeping, citing EO 14281 and the DOJ opinion. A public hearing was held 2026-08-11; comments closed 2026-08-24 with 2,856 received. The EEO-1 remains in effect until a final rule issues.
OPM publishes an interim final rule removing references to the Uniform Guidelines on Employee Selection Procedures from federal personnel regulations, following the DOJ opinion.

title: End disparate-impact enforcement and EEO-1 race and ethnicity data collection
uncertainties: The EEOC disparate-impact closure is known only from a law-firm summary of a Bloomberg Law report, not from an EEOC document. DOJ's June 2026 opinion is known only from law-firm summaries. The Federal Register listing for EEOC from 2026-08-25 through 2026-10-13 shows a federal-sector complaint proposed rule (2026-08-28, read only in part and not seen to address EEO-1 or disparate impact) and a performance review board notice, but no EEO-1 final rule; a title search on the Federal Register (checked 2026-10-13) shows only the 2026-07-23 proposal and a 2026-07-30 hearing notice. A 2026-05-29 multi-agency proposed rule on federal financial assistance (comments closed 2026-07-13) includes a proposal to bar federal awards from supporting disparate-impact theories; its full text was not read. Whether the 2025 EEO-1 data collection ran as normal was not verified. No court ruling on these actions was searched. The Mandate's separate recommendation that an order bar OFCCP from using disparate impact was overtaken by the revocation of EO 11246 (see c18-01).
